chunks.label: Research → What Agent Traces Cannot Tell You
chunks.text: Research paper (preprint published on Zenodo, 2026, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22814181, first author, open benchmark): 'What Agent Traces Cannot Tell You: Evidentiary Adequacy of Runtime Records for Agentic AI Oversight'. Governance platforms for agentic AI compile runtime telemetry into regulator-facing compliance evidence; the paper builds the first benchmark (AdequacyBench) testing whether those records can support the findings of fact oversight requires. It generates 1,200 enterprise agent trajectories spanning 36,296 steps across six determination families, with ground truth known by construction, under four record conditions. Share of determinations resolved correctly: application action log 16.3%, OpenTelemetry GenAI spans 16.3%, governance layer (policy verdicts and article mappings) 28.75%, label-propagating substrate 100%. Findings: OpenTelemetry GenAI spans produced the same outcomes as a plain action log on all 1,200 trajectories; weaker records fail silently (on human intervention the action log answers 52% of cases and is wrong in 27% of those); and an oracle with perfect classification but no derivation relation still errs 47% of the time, all false positives. The labelled substrate costs 4.8% more serialised bytes than the governance layer. Paper: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22814181. Code: github.com/advait27/AI-Research.

chunks.label: Research → Forward Deployed Engineering
chunks.text: Research paper (preprint published on Zenodo, 2026, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22813634, first author): 'Forward Deployed Engineering: A Systems Engineering Perspective'. A structured multivocal review of 133 academic and practitioner sources. It finds no peer-reviewed study of the role, treats vendor and client as a system of systems, and maps forward deployed engineering onto the ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 process model. Three structural properties follow: requirements are discoverable only through operation; verification evidence must be produced inside an environment the supplier does not control; and delivered architecture mirrors the delivery organisation across the firm boundary. It derives a cross-organizational deployment life cycle with six stages (joint problem discovery, environment and data assessment, situated construction, evidence production, acceptance and transition, operation and adaptation) and two loops: an adaptation loop back to stage 2 and a productization loop back to the vendor's product, without which the arrangement is consulting. It argues FDE is best theorized as a transitional organizational form whose eventual dissolution would mark its success. Paper: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22813634.

chunks.text: EADIP (Enterprise Autonomous Decision Intelligence Platform), open source at github.com/advait27/EADIP: a governed multi-agent platform that investigates business questions end to end (plan, retrieve, query, verify, report). Shipped across 12 delivery phases with CI-blocking accuracy, safety and reliability gates (274 unit and integration tests). An independent Verification Agent re-derives every numeric claim before it can enter a report, every side-effecting action is blocked pending human approval, tenant isolation is enforced with Postgres row-level security, and a GraphRAG metric-lineage layer grounds 'why' questions in the data. Stack: Python, FastAPI, LangGraph-pattern orchestration, Postgres (RLS), Qdrant, Neo4j, Redis, an NL-to-SQL safety gate, OpenTelemetry.

chunks.label: Portfolio → Veritas
chunks.text: Veritas, a self-hosted open-source MCP server (github.com/advait27/Veritas) that turns Claude into a rigorous, hypothesis-driven data investigator: it builds and falsifies MECE hypothesis trees over local CSV, Parquet and Excel data in DuckDB, enforces deterministic 'receipts-or-it-didn't-happen' verification so every numeric claim traces to an executed artifact, and runs autonomous opportunity and risk discovery with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate suppression, scored against a public eval suite of planted-cause datasets. Stack: Python, MCP, DuckDB, Claude Desktop / Claude Code, Docker, pytest, mypy, ruff.
